specification.problem: Search for one marked vertex on the complete graph of N vertices using a discrete-time quantum walk in which each vertex has l self-loops (lackadaisical quantum walk), with the phase-flip coin; compare success probability for l=0 and l=1.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful construction: a single marked vertex, the phase-flip coin (Grover diffusion on each vertex's coin space of dimension N-1+l), and a tiny instance with N=4 and l in {0,1}. Outside scope: the SKW coin, continuous-time walks, multiple marked vertices, runtime scaling versus classical search, and the detailed proofs of the abstract's claims.

symbols.meaning: number of vertices of the complete graph
degree of each vertex including self-loops (coin space dimension)
walker at vertex v with coin state c labelling an outgoing edge or self-loop
coin operator on the marked vertex
shift operator swapping the two arc states of each edge, with each self-loop fixed
probability of measuring the marked vertex

equations.label: Walk step
equations.latex: U = S\,\big(\textstyle\sum_{v\neq w}|v\rangle\langle v|\otimes C_0 + |w\rangle\langle w|\otimes C_1\big)
equations.description: Standard coined-walk search step: coin on each vertex, then shift.
equations.justification: Generic coined quantum-walk search form; the abstract names the discrete-time walk with coin but gives no operators.
assumptions: Marked vertex gets a different coin

equations.label: Phase-flip coin choice
equations.description: Grover diffusion coin on unmarked vertices and a phase flip (-I) on the marked vertex.
equations.justification: Common definition of the 'phase flip' coin in the walk-search literature, assumed here because the abstract does not define it.
assumptions: The abstract's 'phase flip coin' means this construction

equations.label: Initial state
equations.description: Uniform superposition over all vertex and coin states.
equations.justification: Typical initial state for walk search; not stated in the abstract.
assumptions: Uniform start over vertices and coin directions

equations.label: Success probability
equations.description: Probability of finding the walker at the marked vertex after t steps.
equations.justification: Born rule applied to the vertex register.

equations.label: Reported success probabilities
equations.latex: \max_t P_{succ}\to \tfrac12 \text{ for } l=0,\qquad \max_t P_{succ}\to 1 \text{ for } l=1
equations.description: Abstract's claim for the phase-flip coin, taken as the target behavior to reproduce (asymptotically in N).
equations.abstract_quote: adding a self-loop to each vertex boosts the success probability from $1/2$ to $1$
equations.justification: The abstract states the success probability boosts from 1/2 to 1 with one self-loop; the asymptotic-in-N reading is my inference.

registers.name: vertex
registers.role: vertex position, computational-basis encoding of v

registers.name: coin
registers.size: ceil(log2(N-1+l)) qubits (2 for N=4,l=0; 2 for N=4,l=1 with padding to 4 states)
registers.role: edge and self-loop label; unused basis states if d is not a power of 2 must be excluded or padded

specification.initial_state: Uniform superposition over vertices and coin states (see eq_3)

steps.description: Prepare the uniform initial state over vertex and coin registers.
Repeat t times: apply the coin (Grover diffusion on unmarked vertices, -I on the marked vertex), then the shift.
Measure the vertex register and compare the success probability with the abstract's claim for l=0 versus l=1.

specification.measurement: Measure the vertex register in the computational basis; success if the outcome equals w.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Estimate P_succ from repeated runs and scan t to find the maximum; for the tiny instance, compare to the exact simulated value.
assumptions: Phase-flip coin as defined in eq_2
Shift swaps the arc states (v,c) and (v',c') of each edge; self-loops are fixed
The N=4 instance is far from the asymptotic regime, so the 1/2 and 1 values will only be approximate
